input.question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't really matter what they're saying. The point is to get you psyched up and excited so you're more prone to buying something. All about energy levels moreso than actual content. If you go to some auctions for more expensive items (luxury cars, art, etc.), then you'll probably hear a slower auctioneer and a more thorough description of the item.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friend are playing a game where you both want the same cool toy. An "auctioneer" is like a fast-talking person who helps everyone take turns saying how much they want to pay for that toy.

But besides saying how much money they want to give, the auctioneer also says other things to help everyone understand what’s happening. They might say:

- "Do I hear more?" — They’re asking if anyone wants to pay more money.
- "Sold!" — That means someone won and will get the toy.
- "Going once, going twice…" — They’re counting down to see if anyone else wants to pay more before the toy goes to the highest bidder.
- "One dollar, do I hear two?" — They’re asking if someone will pay more than the last amount.

So, the auctioneer isn’t just saying numbers—they’re also telling everyone what’s happening in the game, so everyone knows when someone wins and when it’s time to stop talking.
